rubrics.justification: It correctly acknowledges that no image/Gardner score was provided and avoids detailed fabrication, but it still assumes a transferable-quality blastocyst (e.g., ≥3BB) without visual evidence, so morphology assessment is necessarily limited.

It integrates most relevant factors well, including age, BMI, FSH, tubal factor, prior biochemical pregnancy, sperm parameters, endometrium, and lifestyle, and connects them to prognosis and embryo competence.

The reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with a clear baseline prognosis and modifiers. Minor issues include somewhat strong quantitative penalties for lifestyle factors and speculative links without image-based embryo quality data.

Much of the advice is broadly IVF-consistent, but several recommendations are weakly supported or not guideline-standard for this scenario (routine estradiol addition, aspirin, thrombophilia workup after a single biochemical, ERA/NK testing).

Provides practical next steps for transfer support, monitoring, lifestyle modification, and future-cycle planning. Some suggestions are specific and useful, though a few are more speculative than standard-of-care.
